title: Total variation distance as the excess-mass integral
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and suppose $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$. Write $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the Radon–Nikodym derivative of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$. Then the total variation distance, taken as the supremum
\[
  \mathrm{TV}_{\sup}(\mu,
u) = \sup igl\{\,\abs{\mu(S) - 
u(S)} : S \subseteq \Omega 	ext{ measurable}\, igr\},
\]
equals the excess mass of $\mu$ over $
u$ on the region where $\mu$ locally dominates:
\[
  \mathrm{TV}_{\sup}(\mu,
u) = \int_{\{x\,:\, rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)\,\ge\,1\}} \left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) - 1ight)\,d
u(x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ and ν are probability measures on a measurable space Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν (μ ≪ ν)
